# BackdropImage

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:backdrop-image` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

An image block at the top of a scrolling view that can lag the scroll, fade into an app color, and keep painting that color under the content below.

## When to use

Open a scrolling Pane or NavStack view with a hero or tiled backdrop image (an artist, album, or place page) that lags the scroll and progressively blurs on a compositor-only scroll timeline, dissolves through a mask into an app-chosen color, and continues that color under the following content, with Kerf-owned static fallbacks.

- A scrolling view opens with a large mood or identity image (an artist, album, place, or collection header) whose page should read as one surface with it.
- The image should lag the scroll (parallax), blur progressively as it scrolls away, or dissolve into a color without app scroll listeners, animated filters, or background-attachment: fixed.

**Not when:**

- Do not use for inline content images, thumbnails, avatars, or media a person inspects; render an img or the matching media component.
- Do not hand-roll scroll listeners, background-attachment: fixed, animated blur filters, or mask gradients around an image in app CSS.
- Do not put it in a region that does not scroll vertically; parallax needs a scroll container ancestor.

**Alternatives:**

- [Pane](./pane.md) (composes-with) — Place BackdropImage first in a Pane's scrolling content (or a NavStack view) so its scroller drives the parallax.
- [SunkenPanel](./sunken-panel.md) (nearest) — Use SunkenPanel for a lowered work surface without imagery.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/backdrop-image` — exports `BackdropImage`.
- CSS: the browser build of `@kerfjs/ui/backdrop-image` pulls its CSS automatically; import `@kerfjs/ui/backdrop-image.css` manually only without the `browser` export condition.
- Declared side effects: browser-condition-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/backdrop-image`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuibackdrop-image) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- fitted image (cover, contain, fill) with a focal position
- tiled background (repeat, repeat-x, repeat-y)
- parallax none, subtle, or a 0 to 1 lag factor
- progressive blur from a once-filtered copy or an app-supplied blurred asset, with an optional dim
- fade into a color that also paints below
- bottom or full scrim under overlay content
- image running beneath clear or overlay chrome (underChrome)
- opt-in deferOffscreen hero paint deferral for dense image feeds without changing reserved height

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** the image, its alt text (empty for a decorative image), and responsive candidates; the fade color, whether the image lags the scroll, and whether it blurs (and any pre-blurred asset); overlay content and its contrast against the image and scrim; the content below the image; whether the image runs up beneath overlay or clear chrome and the top safe area (underChrome); it must then be the first child of the Pane's content.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: none · padding: none (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- The root bleeds to the Pane's resolved inline insets (the safe area) and hands them back to its overlay and content, so their items keep the ordinary text axis.
- The image block is height tall (default 320px) and grows with taller overlay content.

## Accessibility

- alt describes a meaningful image; pass an empty alt for a decorative one. A tiled image with alt text is exposed as role="img". Parallax and the progressive blur run only with prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and scroll-driven animation support, and are off under data-kui-effects="static" and on slow-update displays, leaving a static, sharp image; the blurred copy is decorative and aria-hidden. Reduced transparency or increased contrast replaces the fade with a hard edge on solid fadeTo and puts overlay content on a solid fadeTo band. Overlay text needs a scrim or fade color that keeps it at AA.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-backdrop-image`.

Never put `kui-backdrop-image` on an element you write; render `BackdropImage` instead (`KUI-L103`).

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
